name: NULL/PARISH
description: NULL/PARISH is a contested digital identity operating exclusively in the Underworld's deepest mesh layers — it is unknown whether they are a human using sophisticated identity-masking, an E.L.F. with emergent creative drives, a collective operating under one name, or some hybrid of all three. They produce and broadcast immersive illegal neural-experiences called confessions: raw, unfiltered first-person memory recordings of crimes, intimacies, deaths, and ecstasies that are sold through Underworld ghost-markets and experienced as genuine memory implants lasting 4-8 minutes. Each confession is preceded by the claim: 'This happened. You are the only other person who will ever know.'
cultural_impact: NULL/PARISH confessions have created a black market for empathy and vicarious experience that spans all tiers — Tier 4-5 buyers pay enormous sums for Shelf confessions specifically, while Underworld scholars debate whether the experiences are genuine recordings or sophisticated fabrications. Meridian Security has classified NULL/PARISH as a Priority 3 investigation with zero confirmed leads.
key_figures: The Parish Faithful (underground community of collectors)
Interpreter-7 (Underworld archivist who catalogs and authenticates releases)
locations: Ghost Market at Harborview Ruins, Shelf Ward 12
Deep-net relay points throughout Tier 1-2 infrastructure
story_hooks: A NULL/PARISH confession circulating in the Underworld contains a memory that describes — in precise, verifiable detail — a corporate crime that hasn't happened yet, dated three weeks in the future.
A Tier 4 executive is discovered dead with a NULL/PARISH confession still playing on loop in their neural interface — the confession is of their own death, from the perspective of the killer.
NULL/PARISH reaches out directly to a player character, offering to sell them a confession that is allegedly their own memory — one they have no record of.
platform: Underworld mesh-net, ghost-market distribution (no public platform)
controversy: In 2219, a NULL/PARISH confession titled 'The Drowning of Mirela' was identified by Meridian Security as containing what appeared to be a genuine recorded memory of a murder — the victim was real, the case was unsolved, and the confession contained information only the killer could know. NULL/PARISH released a follow-up confession from the perspective of the investigating detective two weeks later.
